name: manual_56388c
claim: Python sqlite3.Connection as a context manager never closes the connection. It commits on normal exit or rolls back on exception only when a transaction is open; with no open transaction it does nothing. In Python 3.11, isolation_level=None prevents implicit transactions; in Python 3.12+ autocommit=True likewise leaves the context manager with no transaction to finish. Preserve both transaction and close semantics with contextlib.closing outside the transaction context (with closing(connection) as conn: with conn: ...), or a helper that commits or rolls back before finally closing. Test unclosed connections with ResourceWarning as an error on Python 3.13+ and an explicit leak assertion on older supported Python versions.

decisions.notes: Verified against CPython sqlite3 documentation and CodeRabbit review 5568957759: correct transaction/no-transaction/autocommit and Python-version ResourceWarning boundaries while preserving close guidance append-only.
